claims.body: The Islanders’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Wild’s power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Islanders tonight.

claims.head: Tilted ice, toward the Islanders’ net
claims.body: The Wild have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Islanders near the bottom. Expect the Wild to spend more of the night in the Islanders’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

claims.head: The Islanders’ defense joins the attack, the Wild’s stays home
claims.body: On shots from defensemen, the Islanders are the league’s best, but Minnesota is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Islanders’ defensemen jump into the play.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen last game. Emil Heineman takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L4. Scott Mayfield is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Schaefer and Pelech.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, down from 37% last season.

stakes: The Islanders go in tied for fourth in the Metropolitan with 14 points, the Wild first in the Central with 20 points.

MIN.head: The Wild should be favored
MIN.body: Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. It’s on the Islanders to make it a game, and they can if their power play gets going.

NYI.head: The Islanders are up against it
NYI.body: Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. To pull this off, the Islanders can start with a power play that gets going, plus Ilya Sorokin stealing the show.

story.head: Shabanov meets his old team
paras: The Wild have won three straight. The Islanders are 6-4-2.
The Wild’s power play has a soft target in the Islanders’ kill. The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Isles do.

items.text: Kirill Kaprizov is two points from 500.
The Wild have been without Marcus Foligno since Oct 8, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
Maxim Shabanov faces the Islanders for the first time since leaving.

The Islanders have been without Matias Maccelli since Oct 17, and have had to make do without Mathew Barzal all season. Counting how much each missing player usually brings, only the Maple Leafs are missing more right now.
